post.summary: Trigger a manual rule run with a sync-or-async branch.
post.description:
Small runs (filter resolves to ≤ ``RULE_RUN_SYNC_THRESHOLD``) finish
in the HTTP request and return 200 with the result — fast feedback
for the common case. Large runs (mostly first-ever runs on backlogs
or rules with wide filters) hand the work to a Temporal activity and
return 202 immediately. The activity emails creator + queue managers
on completion.

The peek is a cheap dry-run (``[:cap+1]`` LIMIT, no COUNT(*)) — sub-
100ms even on 10M+ row trace tables — so this branch costs little
even when it ends up taking the sync path.

get.summary: GET /model-hub/eval-templates/<id>/usage/
get.description:
Returns usage stats, chart data, and the paginated usage table.
Query params: page (0-based), page_size, period
(30m|6h|1d|7d|30d|90d|180d|365d), optional start_date/end_date pair
(overrides period — sent by the FE for Today / Yesterday / Custom).

The response is rendered through
``EvalUsageStatsResponseResultSerializer(instance=...).data`` at the
boundary so shape drift surfaces here instead of shipping silently.

Counts and lists only successful runs from the usage ledger
(``APICallLog`` rows with status ``success``), from every source: tasks,
playground, composites, datasets and experiments. Errored and skipped runs
are not usage but stay in the eval logs (task logs, template eval logs);
an in-flight run counts once it succeeds. ``error_count`` is therefore 0
and ``pass_rate`` 100 whenever there are runs; both remain for
compatibility.

Pagination: page (0-based); page_size (page size).

post.summary: V2 re-run: org-scoped, uses V2 Temporal workflow.
post.description:
No manual workflow cancel needed — Temporal's TERMINATE_IF_RUNNING ID
reuse policy automatically cancels any running workflow with the same ID.
Cell reset is handled by the workflow itself (cleanup + setup activities).

put.summary: Update a V2 experiment with diff-based selective re-run.
put.description:
Editable fields: column_id, prompt_config, user_eval_metrics.
Re-run triggers (determined by fingerprint diffs, not field presence):
- prompt_config has new/modified entries → re-run those configs + ALL dependent evals
- user_eval_metrics has new/modified entries → re-run only those evals
- column_id changed → delete old base eval columns, re-run base evals
- If FE sends unchanged data, diffs return empty → no re-run

post.description: Create an immutable dataset snapshot from an explicit items list of at most 10,000 entries and a JSON request body at most 10 MiB (10,485,760 bytes). Oversized bodies return 400 before JSON parsing. An empty list creates an empty version; mutable dataset rows are never read implicitly. Requires workspace write access. Parent versions must belong to the same visible dataset. Returns version metadata; read items through the detail endpoint. This POST is not idempotent: every accepted request, including a retry, creates a fresh version.

post.description: Create or replay a pinned external-task run. Both first creation and identical UUID replay return 200; no task is executed. Tenant, workspace and actor come from authentication. Creation body is limited to 10485760 bytes; JSON config/metadata fields to 262144 bytes. Configuration and code revision metadata are caller-supplied provenance, not executable-code attestation.

Atomically ingest 1–100 caller-executed results for a pinned external run. Identical receipt/payload replay is a no-op, including after completion. Conflicts roll back the whole batch. Finalization is derived only when every planned identity is terminal. Body is limited to 2097152 bytes, each item to 1048576 bytes and each output/error/usage JSON field to 262144 bytes. This endpoint does not execute tasks or attest trace/evaluator provenance.

Compare compatible persisted runs. Requires the same dataset version, exact example/trial plan and selected evaluator binding. At most 10,000 planned and recorded items per run; excess evidence is rejected, never truncated. Tenant and workspace scope come from authentication. Optional include_trial_stability returns per-example counts, observed assessed-score population standard deviations and paired candidate-minus-baseline deltas; deviations are null below two assessed trials and imply no statistical significance. An optional release_gate derives a case-level verdict requiring valid evidence for the complete plan on both sides; a failed gate still returns 200. Optional diff_case returns one bounded canonical output comparison for an exact pinned case/trial; it does not read traces or make writes. This endpoint does not execute tasks or attest caller-supplied evidence.

col_type.description: Column family such as SYSTEM_METRIC, SPAN_ATTRIBUTE, EVAL_METRIC, ANNOTATION, or NORMAL.

attribute_value_types.description: Optional storage-family provenance aligned one-for-one with filter_value for mixed SPAN_ATTRIBUTE in/not_in filters. Null entries retain filter_type semantics for manually entered values.

filters.description: On trace, span, session, graph, and eval-task bounded reads, created_at/start_time datetime filters support equals, greater_than, greater_than_or_equal, less_than, less_than_or_equal, between, not_equals, not_between, is_null, and is_not_null. Missing bounds retain the finite default window: 30 days ago for the lower bound and request-time now for the upper bound. Between and not_between use half-open [start, end) ranges; not_equals excludes one DateTime64(6) microsecond. Because the physical created_at/start_time field is non-null, is_null returns an exact empty result without a ClickHouse read and is_not_null preserves the base window. Valid contradictions also return an exact empty result.

property.title: Property
property.description: Accepted for older clients and ignored for SYSTEM_METRIC graphs: each system metric has one statistic, named by the response's metric_statistic. Latency is always the mean (avg) span latency.

observe_type.title: Observe type
observe_type.description: Population the graph counts: every trace, or only voice calls (traces whose root span is a conversation), exactly as list_voice_calls selects them.

remove_simulation_calls.title: Remove simulation calls
remove_simulation_calls.description: Voice graphs only: exclude calls placed by a simulator phone, exactly as list_voice_calls' remove_simulation_calls does.
